definitions.explanation: Official credentials showing competence in a field.
The status of being entitled to do something.

examples.japanese: {投票|とうひょう}する{資格|しかく}がある。
{彼女|かのじょ}は{医師|いし}の{資格|しかく}を{持|も}っているが、{今|いま}は{研究|けんきゅう}に{専念|せんねん}している。
examples.english: She has a medical license but is now focusing on research.

examples.japanese: そんなことを{言|い}う{資格|しかく}はない。
examples.english: You have no right to say such things.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}には{代表|だいひょう}チームの{選手|せんしゅ}に{選|えら}ばれる{資格|しかく}が{十分|じゅうぶん}にある。
examples.english: He is fully eligible to be selected for the national team.

notes:
{資格|しかく} covers both formal credentials (certifications, licenses) and the abstract notion of eligibility or right to do something.

COMMON PATTERNS:
- {資格|しかく}を{取|と}る: to obtain a qualification/license
- {資格|しかく}を{持|も}つ: to hold a qualification
- {資格|しかく}がある: to be eligible, to have the right
- {資格|しかく}がない: to be ineligible, to have no right
- {資格|しかく}{試験|しけん}: certification/licensing exam
- {資格|しかく}{証明書|しょうめいしょ}: certificate of qualification

USAGE:
In sense 2 (eligibility), often used in moral or social contexts: そんなことを{言|い}う{資格|しかく}はない (You have no right to say that).

HOMOPHONES:
- {四角|しかく}: square (shape)
- {視覚|しかく}: vision, sight
- {死角|しかく}: blind spot
